headline: Adjusted growth holds, but outlook trimmed on China hit
summary_short: Kimberly-Clark reported Q2 2026 net sales of $4.189 billion, up 0.6% y/y, and adjusted EPS attributable to the company of $2.12 (+10.4% y/y), while GAAP diluted EPS fell 32.0% to $1.04 on Kenvue deal costs, transformation charges, and IFP-related tax items.
summary_long: Net sales rose 0.6% to $4.189B as favorable currency (+1.1%) offset the US private-label diaper exit; organic sales were roughly flat, including a ~50bp China hit. Adjusted gross margin gained 190bp to 38.8% on tariff refunds and productivity, while adjusted operating profit grew 6.2% to $757M despite a ~210bp headwind from business exits and a China social-media dispute over diaper quality (independent testing refuted the claims). GAAP results absorbed $109M of Kenvue acquisition costs, $54M of transformation charges, and IFP-related tax charges, driving diluted EPS to $1.04 from $1.53. Six-month operating cash flow was $1.653B; capex was $776M; no buybacks. KMB trimmed 2026 organic-growth and EPS-attributable outlook citing the China disruption, while raising adjusted-operating-profit growth guidance to mid-single digits.

drivers.explanation: Favorable currency (+1.1%) and roughly flat organic sales were partly offset by the exit of the US private-label diaper business; IPC grew on FX and volume/mix, while NA sales fell on the exit and retail-inventory changes.
Adjusted gross margin rose 190bp on one-time tariff refunds and strong productivity savings, partly offset by planned new-product-trial investment and supply-chain spending.
Adjusted operating profit grew on tariff refunds, productivity and favorable currency, partly offset by an approximate 210bp headwind from business exits and the China social-media disruption.

GAAP net income fell as $109M of Kenvue deal costs, $54M of transformation charges and a $107M IFP tax charge outweighed a $39M Brazil tax-credit benefit; the effective tax rate rose to 37.9% from 22.6%.
Mirrors the net income decline: one-time Kenvue, transformation and IFP-related tax charges added $1.08/share of net charges versus $0.39/share a year ago.
False social-media allegations about diaper quality in China hit Q2 sales and profit; independent government-certified testing refuted the claims, but the company expects continued near-term impact.

2026 outlook trimmed: organic growth now seen ~100bp below category growth on the China disruption, and adjusted EPS attributable to KC is now guided to a low-single-digit decline versus prior expectations.
